page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 64 vCPUs and 64 physical cores. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10% to 25%. However, multi-threaded execution is robust; the server achieves strong results in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, Passmark CPU physics, and Passmark CPU encryption tests. Memory performance is also a highlight, with cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth both ranking in the top 25%. Static web serving, Redis SET operations, and Geekbench multi-core metrics consistently fall within the average range.

Given its shared CPU allocation and high resource density, this server offers a cost-effective option for highly parallelized workloads that do not require constant, dedicated single-core performance. The lack of bundled local storage means storage must be provisioned externally. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, memory-intensive caching, and general-purpose web serving. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or real-time LLM text generation, where its single-core performance and shared CPU model present clear bottlenecks.
